headline: A US appeals court has put Minnesota's ban on AI-made fake nude images on hold while Elon Musk's xAI argues in a lawsuit that the law is unconstitutional.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a federal appeals court order on a first-of-its-kind state AI law, issued 2 Oct 2026, text read.
importance_line: Minnesota cannot use its ban on AI-made fake nude images for now, which affects people targeted by such images, the state and xAI; the report does not give the court's reasons and the lawsuit is not over.
summary: Reuters reports that the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals, based in St. Louis, granted xAI's request for an injunction on Friday, which puts on hold what the report calls the first law of its kind in the country. A lower-court judge had turned down xAI's request last month, so the appeals court has gone the other way for now.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); text read from the Reuters wire copy syndicated on Devdiscourse (three paragraphs only). Credited to Reuters. Court reasoning and law details not available.
